info.title: UK Carbon Intensity API
info.description: National Grid ESO's carbon intensity service for Great Britain — open, keyless, no account. Intensity is grams of CO2 per kilowatt-hour of electricity consumed. Only the three PARAMETER-FREE operations are declared here: the service's forward-looking endpoints all require an explicit `from` timestamp, which a declarative producer has no way to supply, so this realm answers about now and about today rather than pretending to a rolling forecast.

get.summary: Current carbon intensity for the region containing an outward postcode
get.description: Returns `{data: [{regionid, dnoregion, shortname, postcode, data: [{from, to, intensity: {forecast, index}, generationmix: [...]}]}]}`. Note the doubly-nested `data`: the outer element is the REGION, the inner list is its readings. Regional figures are forecast only — there is no settled `actual` at regional granularity, which is why this operation reports a forecast and the national one reports both.

parameters.name: outcode
parameters.description: Outward postcode — the part before the space, e.g. `SE10`. Not a full postcode.

get.description: Returns `{data: [{from, to, intensity: {forecast, actual, index}}]}` — 48 half-hourly settlement periods for the current day, starting at 23:00 UTC the previous evening. `actual` is settled and present only for periods that have passed; `forecast` is present throughout, so a query covering the rest of the day must read `forecast`. Takes no parameters, which is what makes it usable from a producer.

get.summary: What is generating right now, nationally
get.description: Returns `{data: {from, to, generationmix: [{fuel, perc}]}}` — the national fuel mix as percentages. The fuels are biomass, coal, imports, gas, nuclear, other, hydro, solar and wind, and they are NOT returned in a stable order, so read them by `fuel` rather than by position.
